I have an 1984 Marlin Model 60 that I recently resurrected (turned out nice) and I wanted to ask for advice on ammo. I honestly haven't fired this gun on over 20 years and I'm not sure what modern ammo brand feeds best in a semi-autos of this vintage.

Also, is there any reason I should not use ball ammo in this vintage of a barrel? I vaguely recall that back in the 80s all we had was lead bullets in 22 (that was a while ago and I could be wrong).

Thanks in advance.
You shouldn't have problems. I have an 85yo iver johnson that eats new ammo just fine. If it's not lead grey, the rounds are most likely copperwashed lead.

Agree. Any current 22 ammo should be fine. I too have several old 22s and have never had any problems. As long as the action, chamber, and barrel are sound, I wouldn't be concerned. The only caveat being ... make sure it's chambered for Long Rifles (LR), Longs (L), and shorts (S). That should be stamped on the barrel, and so if say LR isn't there ... don't use Long Rifle 22 ammo.

Lead CCI are my favorite when I can find the 1070 or 1050fps rounds. That's truly a modern barrel and barring any bore damage, all .22 rounds should fire just fine. Copper plated rounds will increase the wear by a little more, but that would only show after tens of thousands of rounds.

First of all .22 cal rim fire comes in all kinds of configurations. There are gallery loads (often called BB. Caps), short, Long and then long rifle. The ammo comes in many different velocities.

Gallery load is the slowest and has the lightest projectile (16 grains) and a velocity around 700 fps. There is a gallery load with a conical bullet that is known as the CB Cap and has a velocity of about 900 fps.

Next up the scale is the Short which comes in two flavors the standard short and the High velocity short. Both have a 29 grain projectile but different velocities. Standard short is about 700 fps while the high velocity short is about 1050 feet per second. (These are made by CCI)

The Next up the scale is the .22 cal long.(mostly now made by CCI) and come in two flavors the CB and the High Velocity. CB version is about 700 fps and the high velocity version is 1200 fps.

Now we get to where it is really confusing the .22 Cal Rim fire Long Rifle. (They were called long rifle because some of the early .22 cal revolvers would not chamber them. I MAY ALSO ADD HERE THAT NOT ALL AUTO LOADERS WILL DIGEST THE SHORTS OR LONGS. Most autoloaders of today are strictly for Long rifle as they may not feed shorts or longs properly. Also you can get Long Rifle .22cal ammo with bullet weights from the standard 29 grain all the way up to 40 grain and velocities from 750 fps to a sizzling 1700 fps.
